name: Capabilities-Exchange
description: The first exchange on a new transport connection between two Diameter peers. Each side announces its identity, addresses, vendor, and the applications and security it supports, and the answer confirms the common set or rejects the connection.

name: Re-Auth
description: Sent by a server to ask the client to re-authorize an existing session, for example after a policy or subscription change, and answered once the client acts. In Gx, the PCRF sends RAR to the PCEF to push PCC rule, QoS, or event trigger changes, or to ask for an IP-CAN session report. Rx and online charging use it in a similar way.

name: AA
description: AA-Request and AA-Answer come from the NASREQ application (RFC 7155), where they carry authentication and authorization. On Rx the AF, such as a P-CSCF, sends an AAR to give the PCRF service information for a new or changed AF session and to subscribe to bearer events. The PCRF answers with an AAA that gives the authorization result and can include acceptable bandwidth or access network details.

name: Accounting
description: Carries accounting records from a client to an accounting server, with start, interim, stop, or event records, and the server acknowledges each one. 3GPP offline charging uses it toward the charging data function.

name: Credit-Control
description: Exchanged during a credit-control session to request and report quota. The client sends initial, update, termination, or one-shot event requests with usage, and the server grants units, sets final-unit handling, or refuses service. In Gx, the PCEF sends CCR to the PCRF to open, modify, or close an IP-CAN session, and the CCA returns PCC rules, QoS, and event triggers.

name: Abort-Session
description: Sent by a server or agent to ask the client to stop a user's session immediately, for example after an administrative action. The client answers and normally follows up with a session termination request.

name: Session-Termination
description: Sent by the client to tell the server that a user's session has ended, with a termination cause, so the server can release its session state. The server confirms in the answer.

name: Device-Watchdog
description: A keepalive sent on an idle connection between peers to check that the peer and transport are still working. A missing answer triggers failover of pending requests to another peer.

name: Disconnect-Peer
description: Sent by a peer that intends to close the transport connection, with the reason for closing. The receiver answers, and then the connection is torn down without being treated as a failure.

name: User-Authorization
description: The I-CSCF sends a UAR when it receives a SIP REGISTER. It asks the HSS whether the user may register from the visited network and which S-CSCF serves the user. The UAA returns the result and either the assigned S-CSCF name or capabilities for choosing a new S-CSCF.

name: Server-Assignment
description: The S-CSCF sends a SAR to the HSS to store or clear itself as the serving S-CSCF of a user. Server-Assignment-Type tells the HSS whether this is a registration, re-registration, unregistered service, or de-registration. The SAA returns the user profile, charging addresses, and related identities.

name: Location-Info
description: The I-CSCF sends an LIR to find where to route a SIP request for a public identity. The LIA returns the name of the assigned S-CSCF, capabilities for choosing one, or the AS that hosts a PSI for direct routing.

name: Multimedia-Auth
description: The S-CSCF sends a MAR to get authentication data for an IMS user, such as AKA vectors or SIP Digest credentials. It can also report a synchronization failure. The MAA returns one or more SIP-Auth-Data-Item AVPs for the chosen scheme.

name: Registration-Termination
description: The HSS sends an RTR to de-register some or all of a user's public identities in the S-CSCF. Reasons include ending the subscription or moving the user to another S-CSCF. The RTA confirms the result and lists any emergency registrations that the S-CSCF kept.

name: Push-Profile
description: The HSS sends a PPR to push changed data to the S-CSCF, such as an updated user profile, charging addresses, SIP Digest credentials, or allowed WebRTC functions. The PPA confirms that the S-CSCF accepted the update.

name: User-Data
description: An AS sends a UDR to read user data from the HSS (the Sh-Pull operation). Data-Reference picks the kind of data, for example repository data, user state, location, or filter criteria. The UDA returns the data as an Sh-Data XML document.

name: Profile-Update
description: An AS sends a PUR to change user data in the HSS (the Sh-Update operation), usually transparent repository data or PSI activation state. The PUA reports the result and can return the repository data version that the HSS now holds.

name: Subscribe-Notifications
description: An AS sends an SNR to subscribe to, or unsubscribe from, notifications about changes in chosen user data (the Sh-Subs-Notif operation). The SNA confirms the subscription and can include its expiry time and the current data.

name: Push-Notification
description: The HSS sends a PNR to an AS that has subscribed, to report that user data has changed (the Sh-Notif operation). The changed data is in User-Data. The PNA acknowledges the notification.

name: Update-Location
description: The MME or SGSN registers itself with the HSS as the node now serving the user and normally receives the subscription data in the answer. The request also reports terminal and SRVCC capability information, and the answer carries ULA-Flags and the Subscription-Data.

name: Cancel-Location
description: The HSS tells an MME or SGSN to delete its record of a subscriber, either because the user moved to a new serving node, because of an initial attach elsewhere, or because the subscription was withdrawn or no longer permits PS or EPC access. Cancellation-Type gives the reason.

name: Authentication-Information
description: The MME or SGSN asks the HSS for authentication vectors for a subscriber, for E-UTRAN and/or UTRAN/GERAN, optionally with resynchronization data. The answer returns the vectors in Authentication-Info.

name: Insert-Subscriber-Data
description: The HSS pushes new or changed subscription data to the serving MME or SGSN, for example after a profile or barring change or to start a trace. It also asks the node for data such as user state, location, T-ADS information, or UE reachability, which come back in the answer.

name: Delete-Subscriber-Data
description: The HSS removes selected parts of the subscriber profile stored in the MME or SGSN, such as some APN configurations, regional subscription, trace data, or STN-SR. DSR-Flags says which items to delete.

name: Purge-UE
description: The MME or SGSN informs the HSS that it has deleted a subscriber's profile, for example after a long period of inactivity or an operator action. The answer may ask the node to freeze the temporary identity.

name: Reset
description: After a restart, or for planned maintenance, the HSS tells MMEs and SGSNs that it has failed or that shared subscription data has changed, so they can mark affected subscribers for restoration. User-Id prefixes or Reset-IDs can narrow the affected set.

name: Notify
description: The MME or SGSN informs the HSS of events that happen outside a location update, such as changed terminal information, a dynamically assigned PGW for an APN or for emergency service, the UE becoming reachable or ready for SMS, or monitoring event status.

name: ME-Identity-Check
description: On the S13/S13' interface, the MME or SGSN sends the terminal's IMEI to the EIR to check whether the equipment is allowed, for example that it is not stolen or faulty. The answer returns an Equipment-Status.

name: Provide-Location
description: On SLg (and Lgd), the GMLC asks the MME or SGSN for the location of a target UE, giving the location type, client identity, QoS, privacy checks, and any deferred-event settings. The answer returns the location estimate, accuracy, age, velocity, and positioning or cell data.

name: Location-Report
description: On SLg (and Lgd), the MME or SGSN sends unsolicited location data to the GMLC when an event happens, such as an emergency call, an MO-LR, or a deferred or delayed location report. The GMLC answers and may return reporting PLMNs and a reference number.

name: LCS-Routing-Info
description: On SLh, the GMLC asks the HSS which nodes serve a target user, identified by IMSI or MSISDN. The answer returns the serving and any additional serving nodes, the LMSI, GMLC and PPR addresses, and RIA flags.

name: Device-Action
description: A Services Capability Server asks the MTC-IWF to act on a device, in practice to send, replace, or recall a device trigger. Device-Action names the target by external identifier or MSISDN and carries the action type, the trigger payload, its validity, priority, and application port. The answer can return an immediate Device-Notification.

name: Device-Notification
description: The MTC-IWF reports back to the SCS on an earlier device action, for example whether a device trigger was delivered, failed, replaced, or recalled. Device-Notification carries the reference number of the original request and the outcome.

name: Subscriber-Information
description: Asks the HSS to map between a device's identities. On S6m the MTC-IWF sends an external identifier or MSISDN, the HSS checks that the SCS may trigger that device, and answers with the IMSI or MSISDN and, for device triggering, the serving nodes in T4-Data. On S6n the MTC-AAA sends the IMSI and gets back the external identifiers. SIR-Flags select what is asked for.

name: Device-Trigger
description: The MTC-IWF hands a device trigger to the SMS-SC for delivery to the UE as a short message. The request carries the target IMSI or MSISDN, the trigger payload, its reference number and validity time, priority, application port, and the serving nodes learned from the HSS. Trigger-Action lets it also replace or recall an earlier trigger.

name: Delivery-Report
description: The SMS-SC tells the MTC-IWF how delivery of a device trigger short message ended, with the outcome, an absent-subscriber diagnostic when the UE could not be reached, and the reference number that ties the report to the original trigger.

name: MO-Forward-Short-Message
description: Carries a mobile-originated short message from the MME (SGd) or SGSN (Gdd) to the SMS-IWMSC, which passes it to the SMS-SC named in SC-Address. The TPDU travels in SM-RP-UI and the answer returns the SMS-SC's report or a failure cause. The same command also runs over T4 from the SMS-IWMSC to the MTC-IWF for MO SMS towards an SCS.

name: MT-Forward-Short-Message
description: Carries a mobile-terminated short message from the SMS-GMSC to the serving MME (SGd) or SGSN (Gdd), through an SMS Router when one is used, for delivery to the UE identified by IMSI. The answer reports success or a failure cause and absent-user diagnostic, and can ask the SMS-GMSC to retry later with Requested-Retransmission-Time.

name: Send-Routing-Info-for-SM
description: The SMS-GMSC asks the HSS, directly or through an SMS Router, where to deliver a mobile-terminated short message. The HSS answers with the IMSI and the serving MME, SGSN, MSC, IP-SM-GW, or SMSF addresses, plus message waiting status and absent-user diagnostics when the UE is not reachable. With an SMS Router, the answer points the SMS-GMSC at the router instead.

name: Alert-Service-Centre
description: Tells an SMS centre that a UE with waiting short messages can now receive them. The HSS sends it on S6c to the SMS-IWMSC once the UE becomes reachable or has memory again, naming the SMS-SC in SC-Address. Over SGd/Gdd the MME or SGSN sends it to the SMS-GMSC, possibly through an SMS Router, when the UE is available after a requested retransmission or has moved to another serving node.

name: Report-SM-Delivery-Status
description: After a mobile-terminated delivery attempt, the SMS-GMSC or IP-SM-GW reports the outcome per serving node to the HSS. On an absent subscriber or full memory the HSS adds the SMS-SC to the message waiting data and sets the matching not-reachable flags, so it can later trigger an Alert-Service-Centre; on success it clears them. The answer can return the MSISDN.

name: Configuration-Information
description: Sets up, changes, or deletes monitoring event configurations for a UE or a group of UEs. On S6t the SCEF sends it to the HSS, which may also store communication patterns, enhanced coverage restrictions, and suggested network configuration; on T6a/T6b the SCEF sends it directly to the MME or SGSN. The answer reports per-event status and any immediately available reports.

name: Reporting-Information
description: Delivers monitoring event reports to the SCEF. On S6t the HSS sends them, for single UEs or batched into group reports, and also signals changes such as revoked authorization or updated network configuration; on T6a/T6b the MME or SGSN sends them. The answer returns per-report status.

name: NIDD-Information
description: The SCEF asks the HSS to authorize non-IP data delivery for a UE or group and APN, and to map an external identifier to the IMSI and MSISDN. When both sides support NIDD authorization updates, the HSS can also send it to tell the SCEF that a granted authorization has changed or been revoked.

name: Connection-Management
description: Manages the T6a/T6b connection that carries non-IP data for a PDN connection. The MME or SGSN uses it to establish, update, or release the connection with the SCEF, reporting the APN, bearer, rate control, and serving PLMN; the SCEF can also update or release it. Connection-Action says which.

name: MO-Data
description: Carries a mobile-originated non-IP data packet from the MME or SGSN to the SCEF over an established T6a/T6b connection, identified by user and bearer. It can also report RRC establishment cause counters for the UE.

name: MT-Data
description: Carries a mobile-terminated non-IP data packet from the SCEF to the MME or SGSN for delivery to the UE. The SCEF can say how long it is willing to wait for the UE to become reachable. When the UE is not reachable now, the answer can give a time at which to retransmit, and TDA-Flags can confirm that the eNodeB acknowledged delivery.
